Outlet: Yahoo Finance UK live blog, Fri 6 November 2026 (first published 8:55 am GMT, updated through close). By Navamya Acharya; Pranav Kashyap contributed
FTSE 100 today: Stocks slump as global tech rout deepens

British stocks fell on Friday as a global tech rout over AI investment worries after the U.S. midterms spread to Europe. The sharp downturn wiped out the bulk of the week's rally, after the blue-chip index brushed just shy of record highs 24 hours earlier. The FTSE 100 closed 1% lower, almost halving its earlier loss of over 2%. It fell 0.5% for the week.

Key Market Figures:
FTSE 100: 10,673.94, -108.72 (-1.01%)
GBP/USD: 1.3356, -0.0096 (-0.72%)
GBP/EUR: 1.1975, -0.0008 (-0.07%)
FTSE 250: 24,504.32, -197.66 (-0.80%)
AIM: 753.73, -3.36 (-0.44%)
Gold Futures: 4,074.90, -38.60 (-0.94%)

Declines accelerated after the sovereign debt market pivoted sharply into reverse. The U.S. Labor Department reported that non-farm payrolls surged by 165,000 in October, blowing past consensus forecasts of 65,000 and accelerating from an upwardly revised 60,000 in September. The jobless rate edged down to 4.1%, against expectations it would hold at 4.2%.

The Bank of England raised rates to 4% on Thursday and sees inflation peaking at 4.9%. "Markets price a roughly 50% chance of another Bank of England hike in December," according to ING, after all nine policymakers voted for higher rates on Thursday. ING expects one more increase by February, sooner if energy prices spike again. Jefferies does not expect a December move.

Geopolitics: Qatar's emir and Trump discussed efforts toward "a comprehensive agreement," the Qatari Emiri Diwan said. Iran's army spokesman Mohammad Akraminia said Tehran would hit U.S. assets "without considering geographical limitations" if attacked, and that Hormuz would reopen only if its seven conditions were met. The Revolutionary Guards said two tankers caught fire after striking mines, Tasnim news reported. Trump said the U.S. may have to "destroy" the rest of Iran, that rebuilding would take 25 years, and that people would "know soon enough" if he acts. Iran has sent Washington a nuclear proposal via Qatar. Jefferies instead described Iran as reviewing a U.S. proposal, with the sides still far apart. Iran's Mohsen Rezaei met Russia's Vladimir Putin on Thursday, and Putin pledged to ease tensions.

UK housing: UK house prices fell 0.6% in October as renewed inflation kept borrowing costs high, with London prices down 3.1% year-on-year and mortgage approvals falling 19.4% over the same period. Lloyds expects subdued conditions in the near term but no sustained decline.

Companies: MJ Gleeson expects a weaker first half of fiscal 2027 ahead of the April launch of the Your First Home scheme. Rightmove expects 2027 revenue growth similar to 2026, narrowing 2026 revenue growth guidance to 6% to 7%. IAG expects annual capacity slightly lower year-on-year as Middle East flight disruptions weigh; third-quarter operating profit missed consensus despite strong forward bookings.
